15.1_n_plus_one_queries.summary: Two distinct N+1 anti-patterns found: (a) live-mode analyze route loops N addresses → 3-4 execSync calls each, serial; (b) page.tsx fetches roast and compare with artificial 20s/58s delays instead of parallelizing; (c) cache.ts load-chain redundantly re-reads files within a single request.

evidence.finding: for (const addr of body.addresses) loop makes 3-4 sequential execSync calls per address (getAllBalances, getPortfolioOverview, getApprovals, scanTokens). For N=5 addresses this is 15-20 CLI invocations executed serially.

handleAnalyze fires fetch(/api/analyze) immediately, then fetch(/api/roast) after 20s timeout, then fetch(/api/compare) after 58s timeout. Roast and compare are independent of each other — they could be parallelized via Promise.all instead of serialized with artificial delays.

loadRoastBattle() internally calls loadPersonas() which calls loadPatterns(). Meanwhile loadAllDemoData() also calls loadPatterns(), loadPersonas(), and loadRoastBattle() separately — resulting in loadPatterns being executed 2+ times per request, each doing a readFileSync.
evidence.category: redundant re-reads in same request chain

15.1_n_plus_one_queries.recommendation: (a) Live mode: batch EVM chains into single CLI calls where the CLI supports it, or use Promise.all for independent chain queries. (b) Frontend: fire /api/roast and /api/compare in parallel with Promise.all instead of setTimeout-delayed sequential fetches. (c) Cache layer: add module-level in-memory cache (Map) so loadPatterns/loadPersonas are read once and reused within the same request lifecycle.

15.2_unnecessary_recomputation.summary: Multiple sources of redundant recomputation: loadPersonas always calls loadPatterns even when personas.json exists (wasted readFileSync); loadRoastBattle re-invokes the full persona generation chain; classifyPatterns has no memoization; no in-memory cache between load calls within a single request.

evidence.finding: loadPersonas() unconditionally calls loadPatterns() first (line 37), THEN checks if personas.json exists. If personas.json is present (demo mode), the patterns readFileSync is wasted — the patterns data is discarded.

loadRoastBattle() calls loadPersonas() internally, which calls loadPatterns(), plus reads roast-lines.json. When called from loadAllDemoData(), this means patterns.json is read 3 times total (once directly, once via loadPersonas, once via loadRoastBattle→loadPersonas).
loadAllDemoData() makes 8 sequential readFileSync calls with zero in-memory caching. Each call independently opens and parses JSON files. No deduplication across overlapping dependency chains.

classifyPatterns() is a pure function with no memoization. It re-filters trades arrays (profitableSells, losingSells, longHolds, etc.) on every call. If called twice for the same wallet within a request, all computation is repeated.
generatePersona() computes topAmp/topGrd via getTopPattern which sorts arrays every call. No caching of derived archetype results.

15.2_unnecessary_recomputation.recommendation: Add a module-level `const _cache = new Map<string, any>()` in cache.ts. Wrap loadJson/loadPatterns/loadPersonas with cache-first reads. In loadPersonas, check cache before calling loadPatterns. Consider using React cache() for request-scoped deduplication in API routes.

15.3_bundle_asset_size.summary: framer-motion (~150KB+) is the dominant dependency. Fonts use next/font/google which self-hosts and subsets — good. next.config.ts is empty with no bundle optimization. No images in project (positive). Tailwind CSS v4 tree-shakes well.

evidence.finding: framer-motion 12.42.2 is the only non-Next/React runtime dependency. Gzipped size is approximately 33-45KB but parsed size is ~150KB+. Used in Terminal.tsx, RoastBattle.tsx, CompareCard.tsx, and page.tsx for animation primitives (motion.div, AnimatePresence).

Press_Start_2P loaded with subsets: ['latin'], weight 400 only. Space_Mono loaded with subsets: ['latin'], weights [400, 700]. next/font/google handles subsetting and self-hosting automatically — this is correct and optimized. Press Start 2P latin subset is ~60KB but only weight 400 is loaded, keeping it manageable.
next.config.ts is empty — no image optimization config, no experimental.optimizePackageImports for framer-motion, no bundle analyzer config, no outputFileTracing excludes, no compiler optimizations.

Total runtime dependencies: 4 (next, react, react-dom, framer-motion). Dev dependencies include tailwindcss@4, @tailwindcss/postcss@4, typescript@5, eslint@9. No heavy utility libraries (lodash, moment, etc.).
No static images in the project — all visuals are CSS/JS rendered (scanlines, vignettes, glitch layers, corner brackets in globals.css + Terminal.tsx inline styles). Zero image-related regressions.

15.3_bundle_asset_size.recommendation: Add `experimental: { optimizePackageImports: ['framer-motion'] }` to next.config.ts to enable tree-shaking of unused framer-motion exports. Consider replacing framer-motion with CSS @keyframes animations for simple cases (SlideIn, fade effects) to eliminate the dependency entirely — the project already defines custom @keyframes in globals.css.

15.4_memory_leak_patterns.summary: Two memory leaks found: (a) page.tsx handleAnalyze overwrites phaseTimers.current without clearing previous timers, so stale timeouts fire on wrong phase; (b) PaymentButton.tsx setTimeout has no cleanup on unmount. RoastBattle and TypingText are correct.

evidence.finding: CRITICAL: handleAnalyze sets phaseTimers.current = [t1, t2, t3, t4] but does NOT clear any previously set timers first. If the user invokes handleAnalyze twice (e.g., clicks ANALYZE, then LOAD DEMO), the first batch of 4 timeouts continues running and will fire setPhase/setState calls that conflict with the new flow. The useEffect cleanup (line 30) only runs on unmount, not between successive handleAnalyze calls.

setTimeout(() => setState('done'), 1500) has no cleanup. If the component unmounts within 1500ms (e.g., user navigates away), setState fires on an unmounted component, causing a React 'setState on unmounted component' warning and potential memory retention.

CORRECT: useEffect creates local timers array, pushes new timeouts, and returns () => timers.forEach(clearTimeout). Dependencies [currentRound, phase, battle.lines.length] ensure cleanup on re-render. No leak.
CORRECT: TypingText useEffect creates interval, cleanup returns () => clearInterval(interval). Dependencies [text, delay] ensure re-creation on text change with proper teardown. No leak.

Top-level useEffect cleanup () => phaseTimers.current.forEach(clearTimeout) is correct for unmount but insufficient: does not protect against timer leakage between successive handleAnalyze calls while mounted.

15.4_memory_leak_patterns.recommendation: (a) In handleAnalyze, call `phaseTimers.current.forEach(clearTimeout)` BEFORE setting the new timers. (b) In PaymentButton, use a useRef to track mounted state: `useEffect(() => { let mounted = true; ...; return () => { mounted = false; }; }, [])` and guard setState with `if (mounted)` inside setTimeout callback.

15.5_query_optimization.summary: All cache reads use synchronous readFileSync, blocking the Node event loop. 9 JSON files are read per analyze call in demo mode, many redundantly. No in-memory cache layer exists. existsSync + readFileSync pattern has TOCTOU race risk.

evidence.finding: loadJson() uses fs.existsSync + fs.readFileSync — synchronous I/O blocks the event loop on every API request. For 9 cache files per demo analyze call, this is 9 sync blocks.

Demo mode calls loadAllDemoData() which performs 8-9 synchronous readFileSync calls sequentially, plus loadPersonas internally re-reads patterns.json. Every POST to /api/analyze re-reads all files from disk with zero caching.
evidence.category: per-request disk I/O with no cache

evidence.finding: Every GET to /api/compare calls loadComparison() + loadLeaderboard() — 2 more readFileSync calls with no cache. These files never change during the server lifetime.
Every GET to /api/roast calls loadRoastBattle() which transitively triggers 3+ readFileSync calls (roast-lines.json → loadPersonas → loadPatterns).

TOCTOU: existsSync check followed by readFileSync. If the file is deleted between the check and the read (unlikely in single-threaded Node, but possible with async signal handlers or cluster workers), readFileSync throws ENOENT. The try/catch in analyze route catches this but compare/roast routes don't.

No module-level cache map. A simple `const _memCache = new Map<string, { data: any; ts: number }>()` with a 60-second TTL would eliminate all redundant disk I/O. For demo mode where data never changes, a one-time load at module init would be optimal.

15.5_query_optimization.recommendation: Implement a module-level in-memory cache in cache.ts: `const _cache = new Map<string, any>()`. On first access, readFileSync once, store in Map, and return cached value on subsequent calls. Add a `clearCache()` export for tests/seeding. For demo mode, consider loading all cache files once at server startup (module-level init or instrumentation hook). Replace readFileSync with async fs.promises.readFile in API routes to avoid blocking the event loop.

overall_assessment.summary: Two P1 failures (N+1 query pattern in live analyze route + memory leaks in page.tsx timers and PaymentButton), two P2 failures (redundant recomputation + no in-memory cache), and one P2 warning (bundle optimization gaps). The demo mode path avoids the worst N+1 pattern but suffers from synchronous I/O bottlenecks and redundant file re-reads. Frontend sequencing with artificial setTimeout delays is an anti-pattern that should be replaced with Promise.all.
